title: Dhul Qa'dah

segments.voice: Yesterday, Eid al-Fitr: a bath, good clothes, dates before the prayer, and a different road home.

A suitcase lies open on a bed, half full. Two lengths of plain white cloth, folded. A small bottle of unscented soap. A list on the fridge of people to call before leaving: an aunt, an old friend, a neighbor they once argued with. Someone in this house is going on hajj. The calendar has turned to Dhul Qa'dah, one of the sacred months from earlier on the path. Nothing big happens in it on the calendar. But in houses like this one, bags are being packed.
screen: `A SUITCASE, HALF FULL.` → `PEOPLE TO CALL BEFORE LEAVING.` → `BAGS BEING PACKED.`

segments.voice: First, it sits inside the season of the pilgrimage. Surah al-Baqarah says, in Pickthall's translation: "The pilgrimage is (in) the well-known months." Tradition counts Dhul Qa'dah among them, so travelers can already be on the road. Second, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, chose this month for his own journeys to Makkah. Anas reports in al-Bukhari that the Prophet's 'umrahs, the lesser pilgrimages, were in Dhul Qa'dah, except the one he joined to his hajj. Third, packing. The same verse goes on: "So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil." Pack your bag, it says, and then it names a provision no bag can hold. So for some pilgrims, getting ready means paying back what they owe and asking forgiveness from people they've wronged: the calls on the fridge list. Fourth, the people who stay. In al-Tirmidhi, when someone was leaving, the Prophet would say, in paraphrase: I entrust to Allah your religion, what you've been trusted with, and the last of your deeds. Not a wish for good weather. A handing over.
screen: `THE WELL-KNOWN MONTHS.` · `THE PROPHET'S 'UMRAHS.` · `THE BEST PROVISION.` · `HANDING THE TRAVELER OVER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who is going on hajj, or has gone, or hopes to go someday; if no one comes, picture a stranger in white at an airport gate, a little nervous, passport in hand. Stay with their packing and their goodbyes for a few breaths. If you pray, use the Prophet's farewell, I entrust you to Allah; if not, wish them a safe road and a good return.
Dhul Qa'dah. A sacred month, the month before the hajj, when the Prophet made his 'umrahs and when pilgrims pack, settle their debts and say their goodbyes. Today's word.
Your line: the pilgrims set out. And the ones at home hand them over. Tomorrow, Dhul Hijjah at home.

howItsDone: In Dhul Qa'dah, Muslims preparing for hajj often settle debts, ask forgiveness of family and friends, and gather their simple white garments, and families and mosques send them off with prayers for a safe journey.

chat.says: Nothing big happens in Dhul Qa'dah, right? Why would anyone care about it?
options: It's the month before hajj: pilgrims pack and settle debts, and the Prophet made his 'umrahs in it.
It's the month the Qur'an was first revealed, so people fast through all its days.
It's the month of the hajj itself, when pilgrims stand at 'Arafah and sacrifice.
chat.meaning: Dhul Qa'dah is among the well-known months of the pilgrimage. Anas reports the Prophet's 'umrahs fell in it, and pilgrims use it to get ready.
